h: Why Lancashire Makes a Perfect Dungeon
p: Lancashire's past has more than enough dark material to go round. The county is forever linked with the Pendle witches, whose trial at Lancaster in 1612 is one of the most notorious witch trials in English history. That's exactly the kind of story a Dungeon thrives on, which is why a witchy new show feels like a natural fit for the Blackpool site.

Being on Bank Hey Street puts you right at the busy shopping side of the town centre. Houndshill Shopping Centre is close by, the Winter Gardens are a short walk inland, and Central Pier and North Pier are both within easy strolling distance along the front. It's all very compact, which makes it simple to build a scare into a full day without needing the car.
Some handy tips for a smooth visit:

Arrive a little before your timed entry so you're not rushing round from the Promenade. Keep bags small, as you'll be moving through dark, narrow sets. Wear sensible shoes. The drop ride has its own height and health restrictions, so check those if you've got younger or less confident thrill-seekers in tow. Use the toilets before you go in, as the shows run in sequence.
A combined ticket with other Tower attractions can make sense if you're planning to do more than one, so weigh that up before you book.
